statement: Let a be the nondecreasing sorted version of nums, so len(a)=n and a is a permutation of nums. The function returns a result r with len(r)=m, and for every i with 0 <= i < m, r[i] is the largest integer k satisfying 0 <= k <= n and sum_{t=0}^{k-1} a[t] <= queries[i], where the empty sum for k=0 is 0. Equivalently, r[i] is the maximum possible size of a subsequence of nums whose sum is at most queries[i].
preconditions: Let n = len(nums) and m = len(queries). Assume 1 <= n <= 1000, 1 <= m <= 1000, and 1 <= nums[j] <= 1000000 for every 0 <= j < n, and 1 <= queries[i] <= 1000000 for every 0 <= i < m.
